About Me

A little background about who I am, what I build, and what drives me.

Hi there! I'm Anu Mariya, a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) student at the Federal Institute of Science and Technology (FISAT) in Angamaly, Kerala. Prior to this, I completed my Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA) at Sahrdaya College.

I got into software engineering because I love turning an idea into something tangible that people can open in their browsers and use seamlessly. Most of my recent projects focus on the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js) and Python.

Whether it's architecting a civic complaint platform with AI-assisted photo tagging, predicting heart attack risk with a machine learning model, or automating cafeteria meal orders, I care deeply about clean structure, thoughtful database schemas, and smooth user experiences.

Outside of classes and coding, I serve as a student coordinator for our department, which has helped me build strong teamwork and communication skills. When I'm not on my laptop, I enjoy playing chess, doing creative craft works, and learning about new web technologies.

Full-Stack Web & AI2026

Civic Sense – AI-Powered Complaint Platform

A digital grievance platform connecting citizens with city municipal departments using AI image classification and GPS mapping.

Why I built it: When people spot civic issues like potholes, uncollected waste, or broken streetlights, reporting them is often cumbersome and lacks transparency. Municipal staff also struggle with duplicate complaints and sorting which department handles what.

What it does: I built Civic Sense to streamline the entire loop. Citizens can snap a photo and submit a report with their GPS location. An AI classification model (using Gemini API) categorizes the issue automatically, flags duplicates, routes the ticket to the right department, and updates the citizen as work progresses.

Key Features & What I Did

  • Built the responsive user interface using React and modern CSS for effortless complaint reporting on phones and desktops.
  • Integrated Gemini API to inspect complaint photos and determine the issue category and severity level.
  • Developed backend REST API endpoints with Express and Node.js for complaint tracking, status updates, and notification triggers.
  • Implemented GPS coordinate detection and duplicate report checks to save city staff from handling the same issue multiple times.
  • Designed the MongoDB database structure to manage citizens, tickets, and administration logs.

Machine Learning & Web2024 – 2025

Heart Hub – Health Prediction App

A machine learning web application that predicts cardiovascular risk using patient health parameters.

Why I built it: Cardiovascular health factors need quick and accurate assessment. However, clinical prediction tools can be complicated to access for quick preliminary checks.

What it does: I created Heart Hub, a full-stack ML web application. Users or healthcare workers can enter key patient health metrics, and a trained Decision Tree model provides an immediate risk prediction along with record tracking.

Key Features & What I Did

  • Preprocessed clinical health datasets by handling missing values, encoding features, and scaling numerical inputs.
  • Trained and evaluated a Decision Tree classification model using Scikit-learn to predict heart attack risk.
  • Built a Python Flask backend to serve the model predictions via clean REST endpoints.
  • Implemented user authentication and created a structured MySQL database for storing and retrieving patient records safely.
  • Designed the user interface with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for smooth data input and clear result visualization.

Full-Stack Web (MERN)2026

Smart Cafeteria Management System

A MERN stack web app to simplify student meals, daily specials, and cafeteria administration.

Why I built it: Campus cafeterias face long queues during rush hours, misplaced manual registers, and difficulty updating daily specials or tracking student meal numbers in real time.

What it does: Developed a full-stack web application with the MERN stack (MongoDB Atlas, Express, React, Node.js) that manages student registrations, active food menus, daily special offers, and administrative statistics in one place.

Key Features & What I Did

  • Created dynamic React components for student registration, browsing menus, and viewing active special offers.
  • Built an intuitive dashboard showing real-time statistics like registered students and current food availability.
  • Engineered backend REST endpoints in Express.js and Node.js for managing menu items and meal records.
  • Configured cloud database schemas with MongoDB Atlas and Mongoose with data validation.
  • Used Git and GitHub for clean version control, branch management, and feature tracking.
